headline: Direct-sow fast fall greens now — spinach, arugula, lettuce and radishes still have time to mature before the mid-October frost.

tasks.title: Quick fall greens
tasks.detail: Direct-sow spinach, arugula, leaf lettuce, radishes and mustard greens this week. They mature in 25-45 days, beating the ~Oct 15 frost, and spinach can overwinter under cover for an early spring cut.

tasks.title: Pick every couple of days
tasks.detail: Tomatoes, peppers, beans, cukes and summer squash are at peak. Frequent picking keeps plants setting new fruit right up until frost; grab peppers before nights dip near 40F.

tasks.title: Top your tomatoes
tasks.detail: Snip the growing tips off indeterminate tomatoes so the plant ripens the fruit it already has instead of starting new ones it won't finish before frost.

tasks.title: Order garlic now
tasks.detail: Buy seed garlic this week for planting in mid-to-late October. Hardneck varieties handle NH winters best; ordering early beats the sell-outs.

tasks.title: Late blight & mildew
tasks.detail: Scout tomatoes for brown, greasy blotches (late blight) and squash leaves for white powdery mildew. Remove affected leaves and trash them — do not compost.

tasks.title: Keep new seedbeds moist
tasks.detail: Newly sown greens need steady moisture to germinate as the soil dries. Water deeply in the morning; cooler nights mean less evaporation but seedbeds still dry fast on top.
